chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

If her husband dies while he is absent, and proof is established for his death, then her waiting period (iddah) is from the day the news reaches her, four months and ten days, because she must mourn for him in death for four months and ten days, so she should refrain from kohl, perfume, and dyes.
ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period for a widow if her husband dies while he is absent?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the procedural nuance of the widower's waiting period (iddah) when the husband's death occurs during his absence, establishing that the countdown begins upon the arrival of news rather than the actual date of death. It emphasizes the practical application of mourning (i'tidal) by explicitly prohibiting adornments such as kohl and perfume, reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on the continuity of the mourning state regardless of the husband's physical location.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Musa Bin Bakr, from Zurara, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘

When her husband dies from her, meaning and he is absent, so the proof is established upon his death, so her waiting period is from the day the news comes to her, four months and ten (days), because upon her is that she would mourn over him with regards to the death, four months and ten days. So she should restrain from the Kohl, and the perfume, and the dyes’.
en.sarwar: 6. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad Ali ibn al-Hakam from Musa ibn Bakr from Zurarah who has said the following: “Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has stated this Hadith.

‘When a woman’s husband who is absent dies and evidence is established about it, then her waiting period is counted from the day the news reaches her up to four months and ten days. She must begin mourning for him for four months and ten days, thus, she must stay away from musk, kohl, perfumes and dyes.’”
